fact_check.claim: Spring 2027 pre-enrollment runs Nov 10-20, 2026: grad/professional/Cornell Tech Nov 10-12, seniors and Vet Med 4th-years Nov 11-13, juniors Nov 16-18, sophomores Nov 17-19, first-years Nov 18-20
fact_check.note: Calendar lists exactly these dates, all 7:30 AM start.

fact_check.claim: Add/drop opens Jan 19 (graduate students 9 AM, seniors 12:00 PM), Jan 20 juniors, Jan 21 sophomores, Jan 22 first-years 9:00 AM
fact_check.note: Matches: grad Jan 19 9:00 AM, seniors Jan 19 12:00 PM, juniors Jan 20 9 AM, sophomores Jan 21 9 AM, first-years Jan 22 9 AM.

fact_check.claim: Last day to add (regular sessions) Feb 8, 2027; last day to drop or change grading basis Mar 22, 2027
fact_check.note: Calendar: last day to add classes and change credits Feb 8, 2027; last day to change grading basis and drop Mar 22, 2027.

fact_check.claim: Each pre-enrollment appointment runs 3 days and begins at 7:30 AM for all class rankings
fact_check.note: Page says appointments run three days and 'begin at 7:30 AM for all class rankings'.

fact_check.claim: Continuing students pre-enroll for fall in late April and for spring in late November
fact_check.note: Stated on the page.

fact_check.claim: Each advisor approaches enrollment differently
fact_check.note: Page: 'Each advisor approaches course enrollment differently.'

fact_check.claim: Clear your cache first and quit other browser windows
fact_check.note: Page advises clearing cache and closing the browser and all windows.

fact_check.claim: The Class Roster Scheduler lets you save a schedule and share it with your advisor
fact_check.note: Guide says to use the Scheduler to plan your semester and review your proposed schedule with your advisor; it does not say the tool saves or shares schedules.

fact_check.claim: You can place requests in the Shopping Cart before your appointment; it does not save a seat; you must complete enrollment once your appointment is active
fact_check.note: Both pages support this; the cart does not reserve a spot.

fact_check.claim: Course offerings are subject to change; plan backups
fact_check.note: Page advises backup courses because schedules can change.

fact_check.claim: Holds appear at top right of Student Center; some require action
fact_check.note: Holds appear at top right; 'more information' gives details.

fact_check.claim: Permission number goes in step 1 and should not be shared
fact_check.note: Permission Nbr field in step 1; not to be shared.

fact_check.claim: Colleges set their own maximum credits; your limit shows in Enrollment Dates area of Student Center
fact_check.note: Colleges/schools set maximum credit policies; max enrollment credits viewable in Enrollment Dates. Page does not explicitly say the displayed number equals the college cap, but the claim is close enough.

fact_check.claim: Arts and Sciences cap 22 credits in good standing, 18 if on warning status previous term; petition, more than 22 only in serious extenuating circumstances
fact_check.note: Matches the policy page.

fact_check.claim: Duffield Engineering cap 20 credits; petition; never more than 24
fact_check.note: Standard limit 20; 'Under no circumstance' more than 24. Page also says petition is denied for first-years, first-semester external transfers and others (not in article).

fact_check.claim: ILR cap 18 credits; only listed situations (e.g. one extra PE course); no petition otherwise
fact_check.note: Exceptions: one extra PE (19), ROTC, experiential learning credits, final semester; cannot petition otherwise.

fact_check.claim: Engineering cap lowered from 23 to 20 starting fall 2022
fact_check.note: Article states 23 to 20 beginning fall 2022. The fact is attributed to the Sun and is confirmed by the current Duffield page's 20-credit cap.

fact_check.claim: Error text 'Unable to add this class - term maximum exceeded'
fact_check.note: Page text matches (dash style aside).

fact_check.claim: Error text 'Available seats are reserved. You do not meet the enrollment group criteria to enroll in this class at this time'; page gives no direct fix
fact_check.note: Exact text confirmed; page gives no specific fix.

fact_check.claim: Student Center rejects time conflicts
fact_check.note: Error: 'You cannot add this class due to a time conflict'.

fact_check.claim: Do not log in from multiple windows/browsers/devices; can leave requests in 'pending'
fact_check.note: Supported.

fact_check.claim: In step 3, a green checkmark means you are enrolled
fact_check.note: Supported.

fact_check.claim: You are logged out after 30 minutes of inactivity (no link in article)
fact_check.note: Guide supports it (logged out after more than 30 minutes of inactivity), but the article states it with no inline source link, which the rules require for hard facts.

fact_check.claim: All courses have enrollment caps; faculty or departments may enforce restrictions
fact_check.note: Supported.

fact_check.claim: Only a limited number of classes have online waitlists; wait list capacity 0 under Class Availability means none; tick 'wait list if class is full' box
fact_check.note: Limited waitlists and capacity 0 are supported, but the capacity-0 detail and the 'wait list if class is full' checkbox instruction are stated without an inline link, and the checkbox wording was not found in the fetched text.

fact_check.claim: To leave a waitlist, drop the class
fact_check.note: Page says to perform a drop transaction.

fact_check.claim: With an active appointment you can drop, swap or edit grading options, unless consent needed, class closed, time conflict or over credit max
fact_check.note: Supported.

fact_check.claim: After the add deadline, contact your college or school registrar
fact_check.note: Supported.

fact_check.claim: Katherine Yao, a junior in Arts and Sciences, wrote in Nov 2021 that CS 1110 and MATH 1110 often open up during add/drop; mentions Coursegrab
fact_check.note: Author bio says junior in Arts and Sciences; she predicts (not 'often') these open during add/drop and describes Coursegrab. Article's 'often open up' slightly overstates a prediction; attributed and hedged, so acceptable.

fact_check.claim: Email coursenroll@cornell.edu for unrecognized errors
fact_check.note: The fetched summary of the errors page did not mention this address; no link is given. Confirm on the page or drop the address.

beats_top.query: cornell course enrollment strategy pre-enroll tips
beats_top.why: The #1 result (a dated registrar PDF) returned 404 on fetch, and the search snippets show only per-term or per-department guides; our page gives current Spring 2027 dates by class year in the first paragraph, credit caps and a wait-or-enroll plan. Gaps remain: it omits the official advice on gateway courses and the lower pre-enrollment credit cap some colleges apply.
changes: Add the registrar's gateway-course guidance (strongly encouraged to wait for add/drop if you cannot enroll in pre-enrollment) with a link, so the wait-for-add/drop advice rests on an official source and not only a 2021 student column.
Add the CALS row to the credit cap table (22 credits, 18 during pre-enrollment) from an official CALS page, and say that some colleges lower the cap during pre-enrollment.
Note that Engineering petitions to exceed 20 credits are not approved for first-years, per the Duffield page.

fixes: Change the Scheduler sentence in 'Before your appointment' item 1 to say the Class Roster Scheduler is for planning your semester and reviewing the proposed schedule with your advisor (source https://registrar.cornell.edu/students/enrollment/a-guide-to-enrollment); remove 'save a schedule and share it'.
Add an inline link to https://registrar.cornell.edu/students/enrollment/a-guide-to-enrollment on the sentence 'You are logged out after 30 minutes of inactivity'.

In 'Restricted seats, waitlists and full classes', link the wait list capacity 0 sentence to https://registrar.cornell.edu/students/enrollment/a-guide-to-enrollment and delete the instruction to tick a 'wait list if class is full' box unless you can quote its location on a linked official page.
Either link a registrar page that lists coursenroll@cornell.edu in the FAQ or remove the address and say 'contact your college registrar'.

Fetch the registrar gateway courses page (search 'Cornell registrar gateway courses'; the path https://registrar.cornell.edu/classes-enrollment/gateway-courses returned 404, so find the current URL) and add one or two sentences with an inline link to its guidance on waiting for add/drop for gateway courses; use it as the main source for the 'When to wait for add/drop' section.

Change 'often open up during add/drop' in the Yao paragraph to 'predicted would open up during add/drop' to match her column; change 'the best-known student advice' in the opening paragraph to 'student and department advice' only if the official source is added.

Add a CALS row to the credit cap table (22 credits, 18 during pre-enrollment) with an inline link to https://cals.cornell.edu/undergraduate-students/cals-student-services/academic-resources/enrollment after confirming it there, and add a note that Engineering petitions above 20 credits are not approved for first-years (source https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/registrar/).
